sections.normalized_html:
Assuming [MATH: y=e^{\lambda x}] and differentiating [MATH: y] with respect to [MATH: x] gives

[MATH: y'= \lambda e^{\lambda x},\qquad y''= \lambda^2 e^{\lambda x}.]

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

[MATH: λ^{2}e^{λx} − 2λe^{λx} + e^{λx}|= 0; e^{λx}(λ^{2} − 2λ + 1)|= 0.]

The characteristic equation is therefore [MATH: λ^{2} − 2λ + 1|= 0.]

Factoring the auxiliary equation results in [MATH: (λ − 1)^{2}|= 0]

and so [MATH: \lambda = 1] is a repeated root of the auxiliary equation.
